text: Propose by dragging into empty space: create a new graph or offer one of yours, and the owner accepts
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: when you drag from an idea into empty space in a graph you cannot write to, it asks you: create a new graph (and then leads to the login), or propose one of your existing graphs. Everyone can make a proposal, which is their graph. You always go to the graph you want to propose to, and propose a graph there: a new one on the same server (needs the permission to create graphs), or one on a different server.

Across servers, decided by Felix 2026-11-12 ("very importantly"): you enter the host URL of the graph you propose, and the website uses the API at that URL to load that server's graph data. "It's like federated."

Offers go into the guest layer of the benefiting graph (34b3d747); what guests may do is configured by the server admin or per graph (8faf6a70).

Seeing and accepting offers, Felix 2026-11-12: there needs to be some kind of notification system where you see recent new offers and notes. Maybe it opens the idea's edit dialog, which lists the proposed contributions: the hypothesis easy to see and editable, and a preview of the proposed graph.

From 2026-11-11, still valid: the hypothesis of the connection is the proposer's pitch; the owner of the benefiting idea's graph has to accept.

Felix: "This is like intention-connections between open source repos, for the open source repo landscape."

Today: dragging from an idea into empty space creates a supporting idea in the same graph (c3a52342); a link to a whole graph is written on the benefiting idea only, by someone who may write there (supportingRepos, with weight and hypothesis).

Missing: the offer (which graph, by its host URL, offers to support which idea, with a pitch, by which account), showing it on the idea as not yet accepted, the notifications, and accepting or declining. Accepting writes the link with a weight into the benefiting graph.

Assumed by Claude: the dragged-out idea becomes the first idea of a new graph.

status.comment:
Built in e1fc9b7e, 0cc66b41, 3741a2ad and bfb0bba7; completed 2026-11-22 (b5e26039, d4b92ad0).

Flow: without write access, dragging out of an idea into empty space opens 'Propose a space': a new space from its central aim, one of your spaces, or one on another server by its address. The pitch becomes the hypothesis; the offer is a guest note with the drop position. The proposer and the space's writers see it as an unconfirmed supporter ('· offered', dotted, no value flowing); a card offers Accept/Decline to writers and Withdraw to the proposer; accepting keeps the position. A space the viewer may write opens editable in place; requests are routed to the idea's space (utils/idea-spaces.ts), cross-space connections refused. A space on another server opens read-only until the viewer logs in there in one click (1f6f2c46, implemented 2ec19874), then it is writable the same way.

2026-11-22: side panel showed 0 value/cost for ideas of a space opened in place, now shares the canvas calculation (data-repo-nodes.spec); undo/redo cover edits in such a space, routed to it, also for an idea deleted since, an action across two spaces is refused with a message (history.spec, idea-spaces.test).

Evidence: backend guest/notes.test.ts; frontend data-repo-nodes.spec, idea-spaces.test, history.spec; frontend 471/471, vue-tsc clean; earlier probe server with a browser covered guest offer → owner accept and creating an idea inside the offered space. Undo inside a space was not tried in a browser.
